flawed_step: 0009: The claimed equivalence is false as written for a disconnected graph, because Definition 1 permits an empty cut-set, which is then a proper cut-set subset of every nonempty cut.

0003 — Correctly completes the restatement of the requested conclusion.
0004 — Introduces the standard partition-based definition of a cut.
0005 — Correctly requires both sides of the partition to be nonempty, though the resulting cut-set may still be empty in a disconnected graph.

0012 — States the theorem to be proved; no inference is made.

0017 — Correctly proposes considering the two induced subgraphs.

0019 — Correctly completes the description of G[S].

0024 — Correctly defines Cij as the cut edges between Si and Tj.

0036 — The claim that Cij is a cut-set is false in general.

0039 — Correctly explains why such an edge would contradict the component decomposition.

0041 — Correctly identifies δ(Si) with the union over all j of Cij, which directly contradicts the equality asserted in line 35 when several terms are nonempty.
0042 — A page-number artifact; no mathematical content.
0043 — Blank line; no mathematical content.
0044 — Correctly acknowledges that the preceding argument has not shown Cij itself to be a cut-set.
0045 — Begins an invalid proposed partition: the displayed left side includes Si and T-components but omits the other S-components.
0046 — Formula continuation for the union over T-components; it does not repair the omitted S-components.
0047 — Incorrectly calls the displayed sets a partition of V; moreover, even a repaired partition can have additional crossing edges.
0048 — Correctly observes that edges from other S-components to Tj may also occur, defeating the attempt to isolate Cij.
0049 — The set identity Cij=δ(Tj)∩δ(Si) is correct, but an intersection of two cuts need not itself be a cut.
0050 — Correctly notes that these edges lie in the original cut, but this supplies no cut-set property for Cij.
0051 — Announces a minimality claim, but minimality cannot hold when Cij is not even necessarily a cut-set.
0052 — This is a legitimate contradiction setup conditional on Cij being a cut, although that prerequisite was never established.
0053 — A nonempty cut-set’s removal increases the component count under the removal-based convention, and Si is connected as an induced component.
0054 — Correctly states that Tj is likewise connected.
0055 — Correctly identifies Cij as all direct edges between Si and Tj.
0056 — Correctly observes that a proper subset leaves at least one such edge.
0057 — Correctly concludes that the internal connectivity and a remaining crossing edge keep every vertex of Si connected to every vertex of Tj.
0058 — The first conclusion is correct; the assertion about all other components being determined by the original partition is vague and does not establish the earlier missing cut-set property.
0059 — The contradiction can rule out a proper subset C′ as an edge cut in this local argument, but it cannot prove Cij is a bond because Cij itself was never shown to be a cut.
0060 — Incorrect: the conclusion that every nonempty Cij is a minimal cut does not follow and is false in general.
0061 — Consequently, the claimed disjoint-union decomposition into minimal cuts has not been proved.
0062 — Introduces an ancillary remark; no proof inference.
0063 — Broadly describes bonds as basic objects of the bond/cut space, but this does not validate the failed decomposition.
0064 — Symmetric-difference generation is distinct from the claimed disjoint-union argument and does not repair it.
